references.text: Describes the cloud pillar and fire pillar that led Israel in front of the camp, the same cloud pillar mentioned in 14:19
God's angel is sent ahead of Israel to lead them on the way, the same role God's angel has in 14:19
God promises that His angel will go before the people, corresponding with the angel's leadership in 14:19
God sends His angel ahead of Israel, parallel to the angel's protective role in 14:19
Refers to the Lord sending an angel and leading Israel out of Egypt, confirming the angel's role during the exodus
Describes how God led the people with a cloud by day, a poetic rendering of the cloud pillar's guidance
He spread out a cloud as a covering, referring to the cloud pillar as protection for Israel
His angel of the face saved them, a reference to God's angel who protected Israel during the exodus from Egypt
Paul mentions that all the fathers were under the cloud, referring to the cloud pillar that led and protected Israel
Both verses illustrate the principle that Israel's movement and rest are directly dependent on God's visible presence (the cloud).
Both verses confirm the function of the pillar of cloud as the visible sign of God's presence and communication with Israel.
Both verses emphasize that God's glory is dynamic and moves together with His people or leads them.
Both verses describe the pillar of cloud as the visible sign of God's presence, either in motion for protection or at the tent for communication.
Both verses illustrate that God's glory is dynamic and travels with His people or leaves them according to His will.
A theological contrast where God's placement 'behind' Israel's camp represents protection, as opposed to the enemy's ambush which represents danger.
